title: Choose the Content Studio's look
question: The Studio needs its own world, not the Admin Console's. The roll assigned The Class Board. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: The Class Board
options.lineage: the green chalkboard of an Egyptian classroom, and its whiteboard successor
options.thesis: The Studio is the board a specialist writes on before the class sees it: erasable while drafting, signed off before it is shown.
materials: chalk strokes as state: solid, dashed, struck through
aluminium frame, chalk ledge for the main action; a whiteboard-and-marker light theme with the same rules
options.viewport: The setup page as a board: the date chalked top corner, 'Welcome, Mona' centred and underlined twice, the board ruled into two columns (your role and scope; your password), and 'Start using the Studio' on the chalk ledge along the bottom.
options.risk: The most obvious picture of school; it fails the moment it turns cartoonish, with chalk fonts or doodles. It has to feel like a real board used by a serious teacher.

raised.raise: State is drawn in chalk strokes, never colour alone: a solid underline means on, a dashed one means waiting, a struck line means ended.
Coloured chalk is rationed to states and the one action that matters; white chalk carries everything else.
The board is ruled into fixed columns that never move between screens; content fills them, the rules stay put.
Every journey (link, password, 2-step, in) is chalked as a same-scale strip of steps across the top of the board.
Each explanation is chalked beside the exact field it explains, joined by a short line; basics never need a help page.
Every step and state has a name as well as a mark, so nothing depends on seeing colour.

options.label: The Preparation Notebook
options.lineage: the teacher's lesson-preparation notebook, read and signed by the subject supervisor
options.thesis: Every piece of work is a notebook page the supervisor reads and signs in red before it counts.
materials: ruled notebook paper with a red margin
blue ballpoint ink for your own writing
the reviewer's red signature and date as approval
options.viewport: The setup page as the notebook's first page: name, role and scope written on the ruled lines like a cover sheet, the password on the next line, the SuperAdmin's hand-over noted in the margin.
options.risk: Ruled paper is where most tools for teachers land; it can slide into the familiar cream-paper look and feel like stationery rather than a workplace.

options.label: Normalled Jackfield
options.thesis: Every setting tied to its default by an amber line whose stroke shows its state.
options.viewport: Numbered amber lanes on black, each account setting tied to its default.
options.risk: Nobody on a content team has stood in a machine room.
options.case: Clear for settings, foreign to the audience; loses on both axes for an entrance.
options.kept: State drawn by stroke pattern, never colour alone.

options.label: Split-flap Concourse
options.thesis: Rows are live entities; the ruled columns never move, only the flaps.
options.viewport: Account details as rows of flaps on a steel board.
options.case: Strong grid discipline, but the audience does not see their work in it.
options.kept: Fixed ruled columns that never move between screens.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject shown at every stage, at the same scale.
options.viewport: Account stages as five aligned plates.
options.risk: Cream plates and italic serif are the default most generated designs land on.
options.case: Lifecycle staging fits; the world does not.
options.kept: Every journey drawn as a same-scale strip of stages.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: Almost no colour; one accent used a handful of times.
options.viewport: A neutral sign-in with one accent button.
options.case: Clear but anonymous; the team would not recognise it as theirs.
options.kept: Colour rationed to state and the one action that matters.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.thesis: Every annotation pinned to the node it explains.
options.viewport: The sign-in as a force diagram.
options.risk: Engineering vocabulary the brief rules out.
options.kept: Explanations pinned beside the exact thing they explain.

options.label: Cyclorama Dawn
options.thesis: Phases as horizon bands from night to day.
options.viewport: Setup as a dawn: each step lightens the horizon.
options.case: Phasing fits the setup journey; the theatre does not fit the team.
options.kept: Every phase named as well as coloured.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean modern workspace: white canvas, left sidebar, one blue accent.
canonCard.viewport: A centred sign-in card, then a sidebar app like any modern workspace tool.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other workspace tool by design.
